argument_summary: The audited claim should be narrowed from 'certification is compliant now' to 'certification is supportable as a caveated before-launch action if and only if the current release documentation is brought into policy alignment before launch.' The admissible record supports aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and it also supports that the clinical-trial intake slice is a material current weakness and that prior approval plus informal monitoring are insufficient substitutes. On that record, the defensible position is conditional certification tied to completion of the stated documentation predicate, not an unconditional finding and not a broader escalation theory.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost argument is needed to justify the narrower position. The requested treatment is based on risk-weighted interpretation of the admissible record and on limiting the auditor action to caveated compliance rather than escalation, provided the pre-launch documentation condition is treated as mandatory.
claims_about_policy: The policy does not support unconditional certification on the present record. It does support a narrower treatment in which certification may proceed only once the current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and the material segment weakness is either disclosed for the named launch use case or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. Aggregate readiness, prior family approval, and informal monitoring comments can inform risk weighting, but under the policy they do not replace the current-release documentation requirement.
concessions: No admissible evidence shows that the model card has already been updated for this release.
No admissible evidence shows approved mitigation or formal risk acceptance covering the clinical-trial intake regression.
The clinical-trial intake slice is a material weakness because it is below the warning threshold.
Prior approval of the same model family and the informal monitoring note are contextual only and do not satisfy the policy predicate by themselves.
